review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Added 13 temporal relations, each with a quote that states the order: four-unit transfusion one month ago, last menstrual cycle a month ago and heavy menstrual bleeding in the last six months before presentation; recent transfusion before the delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction workup ("Given her recent blood transfusion"); vitamin B12 deficiency before parenteral B12 start ("given her concomitant vitamin B12 deficiency"); AIHA before prednisone ("for the treatment of AIHA"); symptomatic anemia before the two-unit transfusion; prednisone decrease before discharge; positive direct antiglobin test before it "became negative at six months"; clinic continuation until hemoglobin stabilized; stable laboratory values before the steroid taper; discharge and the subsequent clinic visits before the most recent two-year follow-up.
Facts, events, times, flags and evidence verified unchanged against the source; no fact added, removed or reshaped.
unresolved: The source lists no figures, supplements or videos, so no pixel review, figure sidecars or supplement manifest apply.
Table 1 lists cases reported in cited publications; none is the index patient and no facts were taken from it.
The laboratory review values in the first workup paragraph have no stated time; none was assigned.
Platelet, absolute reticulocyte and reticulocyte response values are printed without units; none were added. The serum iron unit mc/dL is kept as printed.
The source reports serum immunoglobulins and complements as negative; recorded literally.
The stable hemoglobin, normal LDH and reticulocyte count in the six-month sentence are not separately timed; no time was assigned.
Whether the three-week duration also applies to the generalized fatigue is not stated; it is assigned to the dyspnea on exertion only.
Requiring blood transfusions in the last six months does not establish that those transfusions were given; the action is unknown.
Home medications are recorded with action unknown: the source lists them as home medications at presentation without stating ongoing use.
Blood product transfusions are recorded in medications; no separate procedure item duplicates them.

key_findings: Single index patient (22-year-old woman); Table 1 rows are cited literature cases and correctly excluded.
Every laboratory value, vital sign, dose, reference interval and the day-5, six-month and two-year follow-up points are captured literally.
Requiring blood transfusions in the last six months kept action unknown; home medications kept action unknown (not current).

Vitamin B12 60 pg/mL flagged low because the source calls this level a deficiency and prints the interval; the vital-sign and hepatic-panel aggregates with normal-except wording keep flag unknown because each includes a stated abnormal exception, which is recorded separately (heart rate 132, total bilirubin 1.5 high).

First laboratory block and the six-month-sentence hemoglobin, LDH and reticulocyte values keep null times: On admission governs only its own sentence, and at six months modifies the Coombs conversion; ambiguities record both.
Hemolysis separate from AIHA; AIHA and pernicious anemia both primary diagnoses; peripheral smear split into five literal findings; Meanwhile recorded as same_time.
residual_risks: Normalize flags OBS-FLAG on the two normal-except aggregates (vitals, hepatic tests); left unknown deliberately.
Serum immunoglobulins and complements are reported as negative literally; the clinical meaning is unclear.
Relations AIHA before prednisone and symptomatic anemia before transfusion rest on indication wording (result-to-action ordering).
